The diff command is: `git diff HEAD` (work-in-progress against commit 0494ea4; there are no new commits yet, only working-tree changes). Run it yourself. Also read the changed files in full: `src/ui.js` and `styles.css`, plus `src/engine.js` for context.

Standards sources in this repo (read them):

- `/Users/leonchan/WorkSpace/IDX-Tic-Tac-Toe/scratch/no-draw-tic-tac-toe/spec.md` (Implementation Decisions: engine/interface seam)

In addition to documented repo standards, apply this fixed smell baseline (Fowler, Refactoring ch.3). A documented repo standard overrides the baseline. Each smell is a judgement call, not a hard violation. Skip anything tooling enforces:
- Mysterious Name: name doesn't reveal what it does/holds -> rename.
- Duplicated Code: same logic shape in more than one hunk/file -> extract shared shape.
- Feature Envy: a method reaches into another object's data more than its own -> move method onto that data.
- Data Clumps: same few fields/params keep travelling together -> bundle into one type.
- Primitive Obsession: primitive/string standing in for a domain concept -> give it its own type.
- Repeated Switches: same switch/if-cascade on same type recurs -> polymorphism or shared map.
- Shotgun Surgery: one logical change forces scattered edits across many files -> gather together.
- Divergent Change: one file edited for several unrelated reasons -> split.
- Speculative Generality: abstraction/params/hooks for needs the spec doesn't have -> delete.
- Message Chains: long a.b().c().d() navigation -> hide behind one method.
- Middle Man: class/function that mostly delegates -> cut it, call the target direct.
- Refused Bequest: subclass ignores most of what it inherits -> composition.

Report, per file/hunk where relevant: (a) every place the diff violates a documented standard, citing the standard file + rule; and (b) any baseline smell you spot, naming it and quoting the hunk. Distinguish hard violations from judgement calls. Under 400 words. Do not edit anything.

1: const LINES = Object.freeze([
2:   Object.freeze([0, 1, 2]),
3:   Object.freeze([3, 4, 5]),
4:   Object.freeze([6, 7, 8]),
5:   Object.freeze([0, 3, 6]),
6:   Object.freeze([1, 4, 7]),
7:   Object.freeze([2, 5, 8]),
8:   Object.freeze([0, 4, 8]),
9:   Object.freeze([2, 4, 6]),
10: ]);
11: 
12: const EMPTY_BOARD = Object.freeze(new Array(9).fill(null));
13: 
14: function countMarks(cells) {
15:   let count = 0;
16:   for (const cell of cells) {
17:     if (cell !== null) count += 1;
18:   }
19:   return count;
20: }
21: 
22: function findLine(cells, mark) {
23:   for (const line of LINES) {
24:     const [a, b, c] = line;
25:     if (cells[a] === mark && cells[b] === mark && cells[c] === mark) return line;
26:   }
27:   return null;
28: }
29: 
30: export function createGame() {
31:   return Object.freeze({ cells: EMPTY_BOARD });
32: }
33: 
34: export function board(state) {
35:   return state.cells;
36: }
37: 
38: export function currentPlayer(state) {
39:   return countMarks(state.cells) % 2 === 0 ? 'X' : 'O';
40: }
41: 
42: export function legalMoves(state) {
43:   if (status(state).over) return [];
44:   const moves = [];
45:   for (let cell = 0; cell < 9; cell += 1) {
46:     if (state.cells[cell] === null) moves.push(cell);
47:   }
48:   return moves;
49: }
50: 
51: export function applyMove(state, cell) {
52:   if (!Number.isInteger(cell) || cell < 0 || cell > 8) {
53:     throw new RangeError(`Illegal move: ${cell} is not a cell`);
54:   }
55:   if (status(state).over) {
56:     throw new Error('Illegal move: the game is over');
57:   }
58:   if (state.cells[cell] !== null) {
59:     throw new Error(`Illegal move: cell ${cell} is already occupied`);
60:   }
61:   const cells = state.cells.slice();
62:   cells[cell] = currentPlayer(state);
63:   return Object.freeze({ cells: Object.freeze(cells) });
64: }
65: 
66: export function status(state) {
67:   const moveCount = countMarks(state.cells);
68:   const xLine = findLine(state.cells, 'X');
69:   const oLine = findLine(state.cells, 'O');
70: 
71:   if (xLine !== null || oLine !== null) {
72:     return Object.freeze({
73:       over: true,
74:       winner: xLine !== null ? 'X' : 'O',
75:       reason: 'line',
76:       line: xLine !== null ? xLine : oLine,
77:       moveCount,
78:     });
79:   }
80: 
81:   if (moveCount === 9) {
82:     return Object.freeze({
83:       over: true,
84:       winner: 'O',
85:       reason: 'fill',
86:       line: null,
87:       moveCount,
88:     });
89:   }
90: 
91:   return Object.freeze({
92:     over: false,
93:     winner: null,
94:     reason: null,
95:     line: null,
96:     moveCount,
97:   });
98: }

1: # Tic-Tac-Toe, No Draws — playable game
2: 
3: Status: ready-for-agent
4: 
5: ## Problem Statement
6: 
7: A candidate exercise asks for a two-player 3×3 tic-tac-toe variant in which a game can never
8: end in a draw and every line of play terminates. The rule has been chosen and stated
9: (`docs/RULES.md`), and the exhaustive evidence that it works has been recorded
10: (`docs/research/no-draw-variants.md`), but there is no game to play and no design document
11: arguing that the implementation matches the rule. A reviewer opening the repo can read a rule
12: but cannot play it, and cannot see why it is correct.
13: 
14: ## Solution
15: 
16: A static, dependency-free browser game that implements the stated variant exactly: X moves
17: first, three of a player's own marks in a line is a line win, and a **fill win** goes to O when
18: the board fills with no line. A line completed on the ninth move still wins outright. A draw is
19: not a reachable outcome, and the interface cannot present one.
20: 
21: All rule logic lives in a single pure, DOM-free engine module; the interface layer only renders
22: the board and the engine's status and forwards clicks. A winning line is highlighted, and a fill
23: win is presented distinctly from a line win so the variant is visible in play. `docs/DESIGN.md`
24: records the reading of the brief, the rejected rule sets, and the argument that draws are
25: impossible and play always terminates.
26: 
27: ## User Stories
28: 
29: 1. As a player, I want to take turns placing marks on a 3×3 board, so that I can play a game of
30:    tic-tac-toe.
31: 2. As X, I want to move first, so that the game follows tic-tac-toe convention.
32: 3. As a player, I want to place my mark in any empty cell, so that I can pursue a line.
33: 4. As a player, I want the game to refuse a mark on an occupied cell, so that I cannot overwrite
34:    an existing mark.
35: 5. As a player, I want to see whose turn it is, so that I know when to move.
36: 6. As a player, I want to win by completing a line of three of my own marks, so that I get the
37:    standard tic-tac-toe win.
38: 7. As X, I want a line I complete on the ninth move to win outright, so that the fill rule never
39:    steals a win I have earned.
40: 8. As O, I want to win when the board fills with no line, so that a lineless full board still
41:    produces a winner.
42: 9. As a player, I want the game to announce the winner, so that I know the game has ended.
43: 10. As a player, I want the announcement to say whether the game ended in a line win or a fill
44:     win, so that I can see the variant working rather than taking it on faith.
45: 11. As a player, I want the winning line highlighted when a line win occurs, so that I can see
46:     why the game ended.
47: 12. As a player, I want a fill win to look different from a line win, so that I can tell there
48:     was no line at all.
49: 13. As a player, I want to start a new game, so that I can play again after a game ends.
50: 14. As a player, I want a new game to reset the board completely, so that no marks carry over.
51: 15. As a player, I want to be unable to place a mark after the game has ended, so that a
52:     terminal position cannot change.
53: 16. As a player, I want never to see a draw, because the variant guarantees every game has a
54:     winner.
55: 17. As a player, I want every game to end within nine moves, so that play always terminates.
56: 18. As the candidate, I want the rules stated plainly enough for a stranger to play from a
57:     printed copy, so that the variant needs no reference to the code.
58: 19. As the candidate, I want the engine to be the only place rules live, so that the interface
59:     layer cannot contradict the rule or drift from it.
60: 20. As the candidate, I want the engine to be pure and DOM-free, so that its behaviour can be
61:     reasoned about in isolation from rendering.
62: 21. As the candidate, I want the engine's state to be immutable, so that a move produces a new
63:     position and earlier positions cannot be corrupted.
64: 22. As the candidate, I want an illegal move to throw rather than be silently ignored, so that
65:     mistakes surface instead of hiding.
66: 23. As the candidate, I want terminal states to have no legal moves, so that the engine itself
67:     makes continuing a finished game impossible.
68: 24. As the reviewer, I want `docs/DESIGN.md` to record my reading of the brief and the
69:     ambiguities I resolved, so that my decisions are defensible without me in the room.
70: 25. As the reviewer, I want `docs/DESIGN.md` to list the rule sets I considered and rejected,
71:     with reasons and measured numbers, so that the chosen rule is visibly a considered choice.
72: 26. As the reviewer, I want `docs/DESIGN.md` to argue that draws are impossible and that play
73:     always terminates, backed by the exhaustive enumeration already in the repo, so that the
74:     correctness claim is supported rather than asserted.
75: 27. As the reviewer, I want `docs/DESIGN.md` to state anything that is broken or unfinished, so
76:     that I am not misled about the state of the work.
77: 28. As the candidate, I want the ADR to record why a lineless full board is awarded to O, so
78:     that the most surprising part of the rule is explained to future readers.
79: 29. As an agent working on this repo, I want `AGENTS.md` to state how to run the game and the
80:     conventions to follow, so that future sessions respect the engine/interface seam.
81: 30. As an agent working on this repo, I want the glossary in `CONTEXT.md`, so that I name domain
82:     concepts consistently with the rest of the project.
83: 31. As a reviewer, I want to run the game with a static server and no build step, so that
84:     trying it out takes one command.
85: 32. As a reviewer, I want the game to work in current Chrome with no dependencies or network
86:     calls, so that nothing needs installing.
87: 
88: ## Implementation Decisions
89: 
90: - **Rule authority.** `docs/RULES.md` remains the single source of truth. The engine encodes
91:   that rule and nothing else; if the rule changes, `docs/RULES.md` changes first.
92: - **One engine module, pure and DOM-free.** It owns every rule decision: legal moves, turn
93:   order, line wins, the fill win, and the precedence of a ninth-move line over the fill rule.
94:   It is an ESM module, browser-only, with immutable state transitions.
95: - **Engine interface contract** (from the design session; the exact shape encodes decisions that
96:   prose would blur):
97: 
98:   ```
99:   createGame()                      -> State
100:   board(state)                      -> ReadonlyArray<'X' | 'O' | null>
101:   currentPlayer(state)              -> 'X' | 'O'
102:   legalMoves(state)                 -> number[]            // empty iff terminal
103:   applyMove(state, cell)            -> State               // immutable; throws on illegal
104:   status(state)                     -> {
105:                                          over: boolean,
106:                                          winner: 'X' | 'O' | null,
107:                                          reason: 'line' | 'fill' | null,
108:                                          line: [number, number, number] | null,
109:                                          moveCount: number
110:                                        }
111:   ```
112: 
113:   `State` is opaque to the interface layer, which must not read it directly. `reason: 'fill'`
114:   can only ever accompany a win by O. `line` holds the three cells of a line win and drives the
115:   highlight; it is `null` for a fill win.
116: - **One interface module, no logic.** It renders the board from `board(state)`, renders whose
117:   turn it is from `currentPlayer(state)`, forwards clicks to `applyMove`, and renders the
118:   result from `status(state)`. It performs no rule check of any kind — in particular it does not
119:   decide whether a move is legal or who has won.
120: - **Winning-line highlight** is driven entirely by `status.line`. A fill win gets a distinct
121:   treatment (the whole board is indicated as full with no line) so the two endings are visually
122:   different.
123: - **New Game** calls `createGame()` for a fresh State; there is no separate reset path.
124: - **Illegal clicks** (occupied or terminal cells) must not mutate state; the interface ignores
125:   them and the engine's `applyMove` throws if one is ever attempted.
126: - **No build step, no dependencies, no network, no backend.** Browser-only ESM served by
127:   `python3 -m http.server`. No transpiling or polyfills; current Chrome only.
128: - **Documentation deliverables.** `docs/DESIGN.md` is written to cover the brief's four required
129:   areas: reading of the brief and ambiguities resolved; rejected rule sets and why; the
130:   no-draw and termination argument; and known unfinished work. The argument is informal prose
131:   that cites the exhaustive enumeration already committed under `docs/research/`.
132: - **Already produced by the design phase, not part of this spec's tickets:** `docs/RULES.md`,
133:   `docs/research/no-draw-variants.md`, `CONTEXT.md`, `docs/adr/0001-lineless-full-board-awarded-to-o.md`,
134:   `AGENTS.md`, and the issue-tracker configuration under `docs/agents/`.
135: 
136: ## Testing Decisions
137: 
138: - **What makes a good test here:** one that asserts externally observable engine behaviour over
139:   the real reachable game tree, never internal representation. A test that inspects a State's
140:   internals, or that re-derives a rule, is testing implementation detail and is wrong.
141: - **No automated test runner is introduced.** By decision, the correctness argument is informal
142:   prose in `docs/DESIGN.md`, backed by the exhaustive enumeration of the *rule* already recorded
143:   in `docs/research/no-draw-variants.md` (all 255,168 lines of play, zero draws, maximum length
144:   9). The brief does not score test coverage beyond what supports this argument.
145: - **The one seam** is the engine's public interface above. It is the highest seam available —
146:   the interface module is deliberately logic-free, so there is nothing meaningful to assert
147:   there. If automated verification is ever added, it targets this seam and nothing else,
148:   exhaustively: walk every legal line of play from `createGame()` via `legalMoves`/`applyMove`
149:   and assert that every terminal state has a non-null `winner`, that `legalMoves` is empty at
150:   terminal states, and that no line of play exceeds nine moves.
151: - **Prior art:** the Python exhaustive solver embedded in `docs/research/no-draw-variants.md`
152:   is the model for such a check, and the numbers `docs/DESIGN.md` cites.
153: 
154: ## Out of Scope
155: 
156: - A computer opponent. Explicitly optional and not scored by the brief.
157: - Undo, move history, running score, and any multi-game tracking.
158: - Visual polish: animation, sound, responsive layout, and accessibility work are not scored.
159: - Automated tests and any test runner or Node tooling.
160: - Transcript export, `transcript/README.md`, and commit boundaries — handled by the candidate
161:   outside this spec; commits are made per ticket.
162: - Changes to the rule itself. The rule is frozen in `docs/RULES.md`; this spec implements it.
163: 
164: ## Further Notes
165: 
166: - **Why the fill win goes to O** is recorded in ADR-0001. In short: keeping the standard line
167:   win forces a decision on the lineless full board, and awarding it to O is the smallest change
168:   with the best casual balance. Because X moves first and nine is odd, the ninth move is always
169:   X's, so "the board fills with no line, O wins" is equivalently "the ninth move loses".
170: - **Perfect-play balance is impossible** in any no-draw variant: Zermelo determinacy means
171:   exactly one player has a forced win. Under this rule that player is O. "Balance" is therefore
172:   claimed only empirically — X 58.5% / O 41.5% under uniform random play — and `docs/DESIGN.md`
173:   must not overclaim it.
174: - **Termination is structural, not probabilistic:** every move occupies one previously empty
175:   cell, with no passing, capture, or removal, so the game is a DAG graded by mark count and
176:   cannot exceed nine moves.
177: - The 16 historically drawn full boards are reclassified as fill wins for O; all 16 are
178:   reachable in normal play.
179: - The engine must be able to represent only terminal positions that have a winner; a draw is not
180:   a runtime concept in this project (see `CONTEXT.md`).

(End of file - total 180 lines)
</content>

   tic-tac-toe.
2. As X, I want to move first, so that the game follows tic-tac-toe convention.
3. As a player, I want to place my mark in any empty cell, so that I can pursue a line.
4. As a player, I want the game to refuse a mark on an occupied cell, so that I cannot overwrite
   an existing mark.
5. As a player, I want to see whose turn it is, so that I know when to move.
6. As a player, I want to win by completing a line of three of my own marks, so that I get the
   standard tic-tac-toe win.
7. As X, I want a line I complete on the ninth move to win outright, so that the fill rule never
   steals a win I have earned.
8. As O, I want to win when the board fills with no line, so that a lineless full board still
   produces a winner.
9. As a player, I want the game to announce the winner, so that I know the game has ended.
10. As a player, I want the announcement to say whether the game ended in a line win or a fill
    win, so that I can see the variant working rather than taking it on faith.
11. As a player, I want the winning line highlighted when a line win occurs, so that I can see
    why the game ended.
12. As a player, I want a fill win to look different from a line win, so that I can tell there
    was no line at all.
13. As a player, I want to start a new game, so that I can play again after a game ends.
14. As a player, I want a new game to reset the board completely, so that no marks carry over.
15. As a player, I want to be unable to place a mark after the game has ended, so that a
    terminal position cannot change.
16. As a player, I want never to see a draw, because the variant guarantees every game has a
    winner.
17. As a player, I want every game to end within nine moves, so that play always terminates.
18. As the candidate, I want the rules stated plainly enough for a stranger to play from a
    printed copy, so that the variant needs no reference to the code.
19. As the candidate, I want the engine to be the only place rules live, so that the interface
    layer cannot contradict the rule or drift from it.
20. As the candidate, I want the engine to be pure and DOM-free, so that its behaviour can be
    reasoned about in isolation from rendering.
21. As the candidate, I want the engine's state to be immutable, so that a move produces a new
    position and earlier positions cannot be corrupted.
22. As the candidate, I want an illegal move to throw rather than be silently ignored, so that
    mistakes surface instead of hiding.
23. As the candidate, I want terminal states to have no legal moves, so that the engine itself
    makes continuing a finished game impossible.
24. As the reviewer, I want `docs/DESIGN.md` to record my reading of the brief and the
    ambiguities I resolved, so that my decisions are defensible without me in the room.
25. As the reviewer, I want `docs/DESIGN.md` to list the rule sets I considered and rejected,
    with reasons and measured numbers, so that the chosen rule is visibly a considered choice.
26. As the reviewer, I want `docs/DESIGN.md` to argue that draws are impossible and that play
    always terminates, backed by the exhaustive enumeration already in the repo, so that the
    correctness claim is supported rather than asserted.
27. As the reviewer, I want `docs/DESIGN.md` to state anything that is broken or unfinished, so
    that I am not misled about the state of the work.
28. As the candidate, I want the ADR to record why a lineless full board is awarded to O, so
    that the most surprising part of the rule is explained to future readers.
29. As an agent working on this repo, I want `AGENTS.md` to state how to run the game and the
    conventions to follow, so that future sessions respect the engine/interface seam.
30. As an agent working on this repo, I want the glossary in `CONTEXT.md`, so that I name domain
    concepts consistently with the rest of the project.
31. As a reviewer, I want to run the game with a static server and no build step, so that
    trying it out takes one command.
32. As a reviewer, I want the game to work in current Chrome with no dependencies or network
    calls, so that nothing needs installing.

## Implementation Decisions

- **Rule authority.** `docs/RULES.md` remains the single source of truth. The engine encodes
  that rule and nothing else; if the rule changes, `docs/RULES.md` changes first.
- **One engine module, pure and DOM-free.** It owns every rule decision: legal moves, turn
  order, line wins, the fill win, and the precedence of a ninth-move line over the fill rule.
  It is an ESM module, browser-only, with immutable state transitions.
- **Engine interface contract** (from the design session; the exact shape encodes decisions that
  prose would blur):

  ```
  createGame()                      -> State
  board(state)                      -> ReadonlyArray<'X' | 'O' | null>
  currentPlayer(state)              -> 'X' | 'O'
  legalMoves(state)                 -> number[]            // empty iff terminal
  applyMove(state, cell)            -> State               // immutable; throws on illegal
  status(state)                     -> {
                                         over: boolean,
                                         winner: 'X' | 'O' | null,
                                         reason: 'line' | 'fill' | null,
                                         line: [number, number, number] | null,
                                         moveCount: number
                                       }
  ```

  `State` is opaque to the interface layer, which must not read it directly. `reason: 'fill'`
  can only ever accompany a win by O. `line` holds the three cells of a line win and drives the
  highlight; it is `null` for a fill win.
- **One interface module, no logic.** It renders the board from `board(state)`, renders whose
  turn it is from `currentPlayer(state)`, forwards clicks to `applyMove`, and renders the
  result from `status(state)`. It performs no rule check of any kind — in particular it does not
  decide whether a move is legal or who has won.
- **Winning-line highlight** is driven entirely by `status.line`. A fill win gets a distinct
  treatment (the whole board is indicated as full with no line) so the two endings are visually
  different.
- **New Game** calls `createGame()` for a fresh State; there is no separate reset path.
- **Illegal clicks** (occupied or terminal cells) must not mutate state; the interface ignores
  them and the engine's `applyMove` throws if one is ever attempted.
- **No build step, no dependencies, no network, no backend.** Browser-only ESM served by
  `python3 -m http.server`. No transpiling or polyfills; current Chrome only.
- **Documentation deliverables.** `docs/DESIGN.md` is written to cover the brief's four required
  areas: reading of the brief and ambiguities resolved; rejected rule sets and why; the
  no-draw and termination argument; and known unfinished work. The argument is informal prose
  that cites the exhaustive enumeration already committed under `docs/research/`.
- **Already produced by the design phase, not part of this spec's tickets:** `docs/RULES.md`,
  `docs/research/no-draw-variants.md`, `CONTEXT.md`, `docs/adr/0001-lineless-full-board-awarded-to-o.md`,
  `AGENTS.md`, and the issue-tracker configuration under `docs/agents/`.

## Testing Decisions

- **What makes a good test here:** one that asserts externally observable engine behaviour over
  the real reachable game tree, never internal representation. A test that inspects a State's
  internals, or that re-derives a rule, is testing implementation detail and is wrong.
- **No automated test runner is introduced.** By decision, the correctness argument is informal
  prose in `docs/DESIGN.md`, backed by the exhaustive enumeration of the *rule* already recorded
  in `docs/research/no-draw-variants.md` (all 255,168 lines of play, zero draws, maximum length
  9). The brief does not score test coverage beyond what supports this argument.
- **The one seam** is the engine's public interface above. It is the highest seam available —
  the interface module is deliberately logic-free, so there is nothing meaningful to assert
  there. If automated verification is ever added, it targets this seam and nothing else,
  exhaustively: walk every legal line of play from `createGame()` via `legalMoves`/`applyMove`
  and assert that every terminal state has a non-null `winner`, that `legalMoves` is empty at
  terminal states, and that no line of play exceeds nine moves.
- **Prior art:** the Python exhaustive solver embedded in `docs/research/no-draw-variants.md`
  is the model for such a check, and the numbers `docs/DESIGN.md` cites.

## Out of Scope

- A computer opponent. Explicitly optional and not scored by the brief.
- Undo, move history, running score, and any multi-game tracking.
- Visual polish: animation, sound, responsive layout, and accessibility work are not scored.
- Automated tests and any test runner or Node tooling.
- Transcript export, `transcript/README.md`, and commit boundaries — handled by the candidate
  outside this spec; commits are made per ticket.
- Changes to the rule itself. The rule is frozen in `docs/RULES.md`; this spec implements it.

## Further Notes

- **Why the fill win goes to O** is recorded in ADR-0001. In short: keeping the standard line
  win forces a decision on the lineless full board, and awarding it to O is the smallest change
  with the best casual balance. Because X moves first and nine is odd, the ninth move is always
  X's, so "the board fills with no line, O wins" is equivalently "the ninth move loses".
- **Perfect-play balance is impossible** in any no-draw variant: Zermelo determinacy means
  exactly one player has a forced win. Under this rule that player is O. "Balance" is therefore
  claimed only empirically — X 58.5% / O 41.5% under uniform random play — and `docs/DESIGN.md`
  must not overclaim it.
- **Termination is structural, not probabilistic:** every move occupies one previously empty
  cell, with no passing, capture, or removal, so the game is a DAG graded by mark count and
  cannot exceed nine moves.
- The 16 historically drawn full boards are reclassified as fill wins for O; all 16 are
  reachable in normal play.
- The engine must be able to represent only terminal positions that have a winner; a draw is not
  a runtime concept in this project (see `CONTEXT.md`).

display.text:
# AGENTS.md

## Project

A browser implementation of *Tic-Tac-Toe, No Draws*: a 3×3 variant in which every game has a
winner. Built for a candidate exercise — see `AI Dev Test - Candidate brief.md`.

## Rules authority

`docs/RULES.md` is the single source of truth for the game's rules. Never restate, re-derive or
"improve" the rules elsewhere; change `docs/RULES.md` first if a rule must change.

The variant: X moves first; three of your own marks in a line wins; if the board fills with no
line, O wins. A line completed on the ninth move still wins outright.

## Layout

- `index.html` — the page.
- `styles.css` — plain styling; visual polish is explicitly not scored.
- `src/engine.js` — all rule logic. Pure, DOM-free, ESM. This is the only place rules live.
- `src/ui.js` — DOM rendering and click forwarding. No rule logic whatsoever.
- `CONTEXT.md` — glossary. Glossary only; never put implementation detail in it.
- `docs/` — `RULES.md`, `DESIGN.md`, `research/`, `adr/`.

## Run

```
python3 -m http.server 8000
```

Then open `http://localhost:8000`. ES modules need the server; `file://` will not work.

## Conventions

- No build step, no dependencies, no network calls, no backend. Static files only.
- The UI must decide nothing: it reads state and the engine's status, renders, and forwards
  clicks. Anything that looks like a rule check belongs in `src/engine.js`.
- The engine's state is immutable; `applyMove` returns a new state and throws on an illegal
  move. Terminal states have no legal moves.
- A draw is not a runtime outcome. The UI must never be able to render one.
- Target current Chrome only. No transpiling, no polyfills.

## Verification

There is no test runner. The correctness argument for "no draws" and "always terminates" is
informal prose in `docs/DESIGN.md`, backed by the exhaustive enumeration (all 255,168 lines of
play, zero draws, maximum length 9) recorded in `docs/research/no-draw-variants.md`.

## Agent skills

### Issue tracker

Issues live as markdown files under `scratch/` in this repo. See `docs/agents/issue-tracker.md`.

### Triage labels

Five canonical roles, each label string equal to its name. See `docs/agents/triage-labels.md`.

### Domain docs

Single-context (`CONTEXT.md` + `docs/adr/`). See `docs/agents/domain.md`.

Let me analyze the diff.

The change adds:
1. `winningLine` set from `game.line`
2. `boardElement.dataset.outcome = game.reason ?? 'none'`
3. `button.dataset.highlight = winningLine.has(cell) ? 'true' : 'false'`
4. CSS for highlight and fill outcome.

Standards:
- AGENTS.md: "The UI must decide nothing: it reads state and the engine's status, renders, and forwards clicks. Anything that looks like a rule check belongs in src/engine.js."
- spec.md: "Winning-line highlight is driven entirely by status.line."
- spec.md: "A fill win gets a distinct treatment (the whole board is indicated as full with no line)".

Does the diff violate? `winningLine` from game.line, `game.reason` — these are reading engine status, not deciding rules. That's fine. The UI is rendering.

Potential issue: `boardElement.dataset.outcome = game.reason ?? 'none'` — game.reason can be 'line', 'fill', or null. For a line win, outcome="line". But CSS only styles `[data-outcome="fill"]`. The "line" value is set but unused. Is that speculative generality? Not much. Actually setting outcome="line" is fine-ish, used to distinguish.

Wait — spec says "A fill win gets a distinct treatment (the whole board is indicated as full with no line)". The CSS `filter: saturate(0.3)` on board for fill. Fine.

Potential baseline smell: Primitive Obsession? `dataset.highlight` is string 'true'/'false' — standard DOM. Not really.

Duplicated Code? Not really.

Mysterious Name? `winningLine` is clear. `--line`, `--fill` CSS variables are a bit terse but contextually fine. `--line` could be confused with winning line vs. color. Judgement call: `--line` color var name is ambiguous (line as in winning line? or line as in border line?). Minor.

Data clumps? No.

Feature Envy? UI reading `game.line`, `game.reason`, `game.over`, `game.winner` — that's the contract, not envy.

Speculative Generality: `dataset.outcome` set to `'line'` but only `'fill'` styled. Also `winningLine` computed as a Set every render. Fine.

Repeated Switches: `announcement` has if on game.reason 'line'/'fill'. That existed before, not in diff. Actually is `announcement` in the diff? No, it's context. But wait, the diff didn't touch it. We only review changed hunks. However baseline smell could apply to changed code only. `dataset.outcome = game.reason` plus CSS `[data-outcome="fill"]` and announcement both branch on reason — that's a repeated switch shape? Possibly but across files and pre-existing. Hmm.

Let me think harder about the "UI must decide nothing" standard. Is `winningLine.has(cell) ? 'true' : 'false'` a decision? It's presentation mapping, not a rule. The spec explicitly says highlight is driven entirely by status.line. So compliant.

Is `game.reason ?? 'none'` — mapping null to 'none' — a decision? It's presentation. Fine.

One real concern: AGENTS.md says "A draw is not a runtime outcome. The UI must never be able to render one." Does `dataset.outcome = game.reason ?? 'none'` create a path where outcome is 'none' for a terminal game? No, terminal always has reason. Non-terminal has null -> 'none'. Fine, no draw.

Hmm, but what about `data-outcome="line"` being set. Not used. Not a violation.

Now consider: the fill-win presentation uses `filter: saturate(0.3)` on `.board`, which desaturates the whole board including the winning marks... but a fill win has no line, so fine.

Another: CSS `--line` variable name. `--line` used for winning-line highlight. Could be Mysterious Name judgement call.

Is there duplication between `dataset.mark = mark ?? 'empty'` and `dataset.highlight = ... ? 'true' : 'false'`? No.

Actually, a more meaningful point: `winningLine` Set construction each render is trivial.

Let me reconsider "Speculative Generality": setting `boardElement.dataset.outcome = game.reason` writes 'line' and 'none' values that no CSS or JS reads. Only 'fill' is consumed. That's arguably speculative/dead data. Judgement call, minor.

Also there might be a standard violation: AGENTS.md says `styles.css` — "plain styling; visual polish is explicitly not scored." Not a violation, just not scored.

Let me also check index.html to see board element exists. Not needed.

Now, is there a hard violation anywhere? I don't think there is a hard documented-standard violation. Let me double-check the spec's "It performs no rule check of any kind — in particular it does not decide whether a move is legal or who has won." The diff doesn't decide legality or winner. `winningLine.has(cell)` selects which cells to highlight based on engine-provided line — that's rendering, not deciding. Compliant.

Hmm, but one could argue: `game.reason === 'fill'` maps to board styling and `announcement` maps reason to text. Both are in UI but presentation, not rule. Fine.

Let me consider Feature Envy on the UI's render reaching into `game` (status object) fields: over, winner, reason, line. But that's the documented contract; not envy.

So report: no hard violations; a couple judgement-call smells.

Let me be precise and under 400 words. Let me also confirm git status maybe there are other changed files. The prompt says only ui.js and styles.css. Fine.

Let me write the report.

Smells to name with quotes:
1. Speculative Generality (judgement): `boardElement.dataset.outcome = game.reason ?? 'none';` — values `'line'` and `'none'` are written but no CSS/JS consumes them; only `[data-outcome="fill"]` exists in styles.css. Could set only when fill, or style the other values.
2. Mysterious Name (judgement): CSS `--line` / `--fill`. `--line` denotes the winning-line highlight color but reads as a generic line/border color; `--fill` denotes the fill-win outline. Rename to `--win-line`, `--fill-win`.
3. Repeated Switches (judgement, pre-existing, extended): `announcement()` branches on `game.reason`, and now `data-outcome`/CSS also branches on the same `reason`. Two dispatch tables on the same domain value across ui.js/styles.css. Since the spec fixes the reason vocabulary to `'line' | 'fill'`, low risk; a shared map would centralize.

Also note the diff correctly keeps highlight driven by `status.line` per spec — no violation.

Let me check: is `winningLine` a Data Clump? No.

Also `game.line ?? []` handles null for fill/non-terminal. Fine.

I'll structure: Hard violations: none. Judgement calls. Word count under 400.

Actually let me reconsider whether setting `data-outcome="line"` is actually used. Search styles.css — only `[data-outcome="fill"]`. So 'line' unused. Confirmed.

Could there be an accessibility concern? Out of scope, not scored.

Write concise report.

Read the diff and all four sources. Findings below.

## Hard violations of documented standards
**None.** The changed hunks stay inside the seam:
- `winningLine` is derived from `game.line`, and `data-outcome` from `game.reason` — the UI reads the engine's status and renders it, exactly as `AGENTS.md` §Conventions ("reads state and the engine's status, renders, and forwards clicks") and `spec.md` Implementation Decisions ("Winning-line highlight is driven entirely by `status.line`") require.
- No rule check leaks into `ui.js`; no draw path is introduced (`game.reason ?? 'none'` is `null` only while the game is live, never terminal). §"A draw is not a runtime outcome" is respected.

## Baseline smells (all judgement calls)
1. **Speculative Generality** — `src/ui.js:44`
   `boardElement.dataset.outcome = game.reason ?? 'none';`
   Writes `'line'` and `'none'`, but `styles.css` only ever matches `[data-outcome="fill"]`. Two of the three emitted values are dead. Either style them or set the attribute only for the fill case.

2. **Mysterious Name** — `styles.css:9-10`
   `--line: #d9a520; --fill: #8f8a7e;`
   `--line` reads as a generic border/rule colour but means *winning-line highlight*; `--fill` means *fill-win outline*. `--win-line` / `--fill-win` would reveal intent.

3. **Repeated Switches** (mild, partly pre-existing) — `src/ui.js:44,51,62-65` + `styles.css:82`
   The same `reason` vocabulary (`'line' | 'fill'`) is dispatched in `announcement()`, in `data-outcome`, and again in the CSS selector. Three places must change if a reason is added. The spec freezes the vocabulary to two values, so risk is low; a shared map would gather it.

Non-issues worth noting: the `Set` construction per render is trivial; `'true'/'false'` dataset strings are idiomatic DOM, not Primitive Obsession; `filter: saturate(0.3)` on `.board` for a fill win cannot wash out a line highlight because a fill win has no line.

Net: clean against the repo's seam; only cosmetic naming/generality judgement calls.
